subject: ventures/translator-project-quote
professional: a freelance translator or small-LSP project manager who quotes jobs from a Trados/memoQ analysis report (repetitions, 101%/context, 100%, 95-99, 85-94, 75-84, 50-74, no match) against a per-word rate and a discount grid, with an ISO 17100 reviser step priced separately

evidence.correctness: Ran node --test '*.test.mjs' in ventures/translator-project-quote: 89 pass, 0 fail. Wrote an independent Python re-implementation from the README 'Model' bullets (scratchpad/translator/ind.py) and compared four unlike scenarios with calc.mjs via node (scratchpad/translator/run.mjs): the README/guide default (2,400 weighted, 435 direct, 580 recommended), a 10,000-word Trados-style analysis collapsed to one fuzzy rate (5,650 weighted, 678 at $0.12/word), a rush job, and a 150-word job where the minimum binds (50). All match exactly. The vs-flat-rate page arithmetic (337.50, 225, 242.50 gap, 300) also recomputes. The arithmetic is right as documented; the rush fee being grossed up by the margin (533.33 instead of the 480 a 50% rush surcharge on a 320 price gives) is a departure from practice, scored under domain.
evidence.completeness: Every feature the README and index.html list works: weighted words, hours, labour, QA/DTP/rush add-ons, floor vs minimum, target-margin price, recommended quote (larger of floor and margin price), copy summary, shareable link, local draft, currency label, printable client quote with scope lines that drop zero-priced items, usage off-switch. page.test.mjs, share.test.mjs and proposal.test.mjs pass. No stubs or dead links found in the four HTML pages. Gaps are scope, not unfinished claims.
evidence.verification: 89 tests pass. Seeded 7 mutations in calc.mjs, each reverted (git status clean for the subject dir afterwards). Caught: floor ignoring direct cost, QA hours not priced, recommended = floor, fuzzy-rate cap removed. Survived: fuzzy weight inverted to (100 - fuzzy_rate)/100 (every test uses fuzzy_rate 50, where the inversion is identical), rush fee dropped from add-ons (every test uses rush_fee 0), and target_margin >= 100 loosened to > 100 (margin 100 then divides by zero to Infinity). 4 of 7 caught; the two most domain-specific inputs (fuzzy weight, rush) are untested.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (75 lines), calc.test.mjs, index.html script, usage.mjs, share.mjs headers. One validation path, pure calculate(), comments explain the recommended-price fix. Defects: in the browser a blank field becomes Number('') = 0 and passes validation, so a cleared fuzzy-rate box silently prices fuzzy words free (probe: weighted words 1,800 instead of 2,400); money() prints no thousands separator ('USD 5650.00'); a 1e12-word job is accepted without a warning. The proposal block is generated from platform/proposal and well guarded. Minor.
evidence.claims: README and every page carry the no-warranty and no-SLA text, privacy statement, and the 'arithmetic, not a recommended rate' limit. vs-smartcat.html describes Smartcat as a cloud CAT tool with TM, terminology, MT and a freelance marketplace, which matches third-party descriptions (Wikipedia, reviews found by web search; smartcat.com itself was blocked by the proxy), avoids pricing, and carries a non-affiliation line; it omits Smartcat's current AI-first positioning but makes no false claim. Fails: vs-a-flat-per-word-rate.html:29 says 'a fuzzy match bills at its match percentage' and how-to-quote-a-translation-project.html:35 says to treat the match percentage as 'the fraction of a full word's effort'; the tool itself uses a separate pay rate, and common grids pay a 95-99% match about 30% and an 85-94% match about 50% (ProZ forum grids), so following the copy inflates weighted words (about 9,418 vs 6,375 on a sample 10,000-word analysis). README:79 lists three usage counters but index.html also records proposal_printed and company_forgotten; README says the proposal module serves '102 bid calculators' while platform/proposal/trades.json has 92 entries and 93 venture pages carry the block. llms.txt links the old github.io host and sitemap.xml uses example.invalid; the build rewrites these at deploy (the served page could not be loaded: proxy 403), so recorded as source-only.
evidence.fitness: Walked the job: a CAT analysis for a 10,000-word file has 6 to 8 bands. The tool takes one 'fuzzy-match words' count and one rate, so the translator must compute the weighted total by hand first (I had to: 2,650 weighted fuzzy words / 7,000 = 37.857%, which the HTML step=1 field marks invalid). There is no per-word rate input (translators and agencies quote per word; here it is derived as hourly/words-per-hour), no repetitions or 100%/context-match lines, no separate reviser rate for ISO 17100 revision, and rush is a flat amount rather than a % surcharge. For a single direct-client job with one fuzzy band it works and the printed quote is genuinely useful.
evidence.domain: Compared against CAT-tool discount-grid practice (Trados/memoQ bands; ProZ forum grids: reps 0-10%, 100% 10-15%, 95-99 30%, 85-94 50%, 75-84 60-70%, 50-74 90-100%), rush practice (a 25-50% surcharge on the fee) and ISO 17100 (translate + revise by a second linguist). Departures: a single fuzzy band; the page copy equates match percentage with effort, the opposite of how grids work; the rush fee is treated as a cost and grossed up by the target margin, so a typed fee of 160 becomes 213 on the client price; QA/review is priced at the translator's own hourly rate with no reviser line or per-word revision rate; defaults (45/h, 400 words/h = $0.1125/word, $250 minimum) are uncited, and $250 is high for a freelance minimum fee. The weighted-word, hourly-productivity method itself is sound and well explained.

verdict: Translator Project Quote is a small, arithmetically correct weighted-word calculator with a genuinely useful printable client quote. Four scenarios recomputed by an independent implementation match exactly, 89 tests pass, and the disclaimers and Smartcat comparison are honest. It misses the bar on verification and claims (both 2, median 2): 3 of 7 seeded mutations survived because no test varies the fuzzy rate or uses a rush fee, and two pages tell translators a fuzzy match bills at its match percentage, the opposite of CAT discount-grid practice (95-99% matches commonly pay about 30%). A translator or LSP PM quoting from a multi-band Trados/memoQ analysis must collapse the bands by hand, has no per-word rate, no reviser line for ISO 17100 revision, and sees a flat rush fee inflated by the margin, so fitness and domain are 2.
